root_cause.text: In `drivers/crypto/ccp/sev-dev.c`'s `sev_ioctl_do_pek_csr()`, the SEV PEK CSR ioctl used `data.len` returned by firmware to `copy_to_user()` the CSR blob even when `__sev_do_cmd_locked()`/firmware reported failure, so an invalid-length error could make firmware return a larger required size than the kernel-allocated blob buffer and trigger an out-of-bounds copy to userspace.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error)) goto e_free_blob;` before copying `blob` to userspace, and the commit/CVE explicitly state that on firmware command failure due to invalid length, “copying the number of bytes firmware requires will overflow the kernel-allocated buffer and leak data to userspace.”

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds `if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error)) goto e_free_blob;` before copying `blob` to userspace, and the commit/CVE explicitly state that on firmware command failure due to invalid length, “copying the number of bytes firmware requires will overflow the kernel-allocated buffer and leak data to userspace.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Clarify in comments that the PEK CSR ioctl returns the firmware-reported CSR blob length to userspace.
intent_record.what: A single-line comment above `input.length = data.len;` was replaced with a multi-line comment explaining that firmware returns the CSR blob length, either the minimum required length or the actual written length, and that this value is returned to the user.
intent_record.how: This change does not alter runtime behavior; the code still assigns `data.len` to `input.length` and copies it back to userspace, but the updated comment clarifies the meaning of the returned length value.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an early error check to avoid copying PEK CSR data to userspace when the command failed or returned an unexpected firmware error.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added after the preceding operation and before the copy_to_user() block: `if (ret || WARN_ON_ONCE(argp->error)) goto e_free_blob;`.
intent_record.how: This causes the function to stop and jump to cleanup if an error was already recorded in `ret` or if `argp->error` is unexpectedly set, preventing the code from copying the blob to userspace when the command did not complete successfully.

grouping_result.intent: Clarify in comments that the PEK CSR ioctl returns the firmware-reported CSR blob length to userspace.
Add an early error check to avoid copying PEK CSR data to userspace when the command failed or returned an unexpected firmware error.

relevance_review.reason: The change only updates comments to clarify returned length semantics; it does not modify the error handling or prevent using firmware-returned data.len after command failure, which is the root cause of the out-of-bounds copy.

The change directly addresses the root cause by adding an early error check so PEK CSR data is not copied to userspace when the firmware command fails or returns an unexpected error, preventing use of an invalid returned length in copy_to_user().

candidates.rationale: This is the direct sink of the vulnerability: it copies the CSR blob to userspace using the firmware-returned length without first ensuring the command succeeded, allowing an out-of-bounds copy when firmware reports an error with a larger required size.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs the userspace copy of the PEK CSR blob using the firmware-influenced length field without first gating the copy on successful completion of the SEV command. When firmware returns an error along with a larger required size, this copy can read past the kernel-allocated blob buffer and disclose out-of-bounds memory to userspace.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant function `sev_ioctl_do_pek_csr()` is shown with enough context to evaluate the vulnerable copy logic. The root cause is copying data to userspace using a length that may have been modified by firmware even when the firmware command fails. In this snippet, the function allocates the CSR blob based on the user-supplied `input.length` (`if (input.length > SEV_FW_BLOB_MAX_SIZE) ...` and later the blob is allocated before the command), then after `cmd:` it performs `ret = __sev_do_cmd_locked(SEV_CMD_PEK_CSR, data, &argp->error);` and unconditionally, if `blob` exists, does `copy_to_user(input_address, blob, input.length)`. There is no check that `ret` indicates success before the copy, and no use of a safely bounded original allocation length distinct from the possibly firmware-updated length. This means the vulnerable construct is present: `copy_to_user(..., blob, input.length)` can use a length influenced by firmware/error handling rather than the allocated blob size. The commit only changes `__user` pointer handling (`void __user *input_address;` and using `copy_to_user(input_address, ...)`) and does not add the necessary guard to avoid copying on firmware failure or to cap the copied length. Therefore the bug is present and the fix is not.
